summary: Well-executed preregistered pilot demonstrating an autonomous generate→verify→repair pipeline and artifact capture. The pilot produced 50 paired tasks (planned N=300) with both baseline and verifier-augmented pipelines passing the deterministic verifier on all executed tasks (50/50), so no effect was observed. The manuscript documents preregistration, execution metadata, and limitations candidly. Key concerns center on (1) deviation from the preregistered N (pilot vs confirmatory), (2) lack of an explicit model identifier in the paper text (referenced only via an archived artifact), and (3) insufficient specification and validation of the deterministic verifier and task difficulty (risk that tasks/verifier are trivial or verifier too permissive). If these issues are addressed (full disclosure of model identifier or an explicit, track-compliant justification; formal verifier specification and representative task/output examples; contamination/audit summary and artifact access instructions), the paper is appropriate as a short-track pilot report for the Agentic AI Researcher session.
critical_issues: Preregistered confirmatory N=300 was not met; only a 50-task scientific_pilot was executed. This underpowers the confirmatory claim and prevents analysis of repair behaviour — the deviation is reported but must be highlighted and justified in the manuscript as a deliberate pilot rather than a confirmation.

The Disclosure Statement does not present the exact LLM model identifier in the manuscript body; it points to an archived artifact containing that identifier. The track requires disclosure of LLM(s) and exact model identifiers where available — the manuscript must either include the identifier (preferred) or provide an explicit, auditable reason consistent with conference policy for withholding it.

Deterministic verifier is insufficiently specified in the manuscript. The paper lacks a formal description of verifier semantics, assertion types checked, parsing/normalization rules, and examples of pass/fail assertions. Without this, a 100% pass rate is uninterpretable (could indicate trivial tasks, overly permissive verifier, or memorization).

Potential contamination/memorization risk is acknowledged but the paper does not report the planned contamination-audit summary (counts and examples of 'potential_contamination' or 'residual_uncertainty') in the main text; given the perfect pass rate this audit is essential to rule out dataset leakage or memorized canonical configs.

No representative task examples, prompts, or sample model outputs are shown in the paper (even one or two short examples). Readers cannot assess task difficulty, prompt-template influence, or repair interactions; the archive hashes are useful but the manuscript should include human-readable examples for audit.

Bootstrap 95% CI reported as [0.0,0.0]; the manuscript should explain why the CI has zero width (all paired differences identical) and how CI reporting interacts with pilot sample size and bootstrap assumptions.
required_revisions: State explicitly in the manuscript (within pages 1–5) that this is a preregistered pilot and explain why the N=300 confirmatory run was not executed (time/resource limits or planned staged execution). Move the current note from Discussion to a clear, prominent statement in Introduction and Disclosure.

Include the exact LLM model identifier(s) and provider name(s) in the Disclosure Statement (or provide an auditable justification, consistent with venue rules, for nondisclosure). Also include the model configuration file path and its artifact hash for verification.

Add a formal specification of the deterministic verifier: grammar/semantic checks, assertion taxonomy, parsing and sanitizer rules, and decision thresholds. Include at least 2–3 compact representative examples (intent, generated CLI, verifier output) in the main text or very short figure/table so readers can assess verifier strength and task realism.

Report the contamination/audit outcomes in the manuscript (counts and short examples of flagged items, and how sensitivity analyses change the primary estimand when flagged items are excluded). If the audit found no flags, state that explicitly and describe the audit procedure used on the run.

Provide brief representative prompt templates used for baseline and verifier-augmented pipelines (the master prompt may be referenced, but include the concrete prompt templates and the injected verifier-failure context template), plus an accessible pointer (URL or archive path and hashes) for full prompt logs so reviewers can reproduce the audit.

Clarify the bootstrap CI procedure that produced [0.0,0.0]: explain resampling scheme, why CI has zero width, and caution readers that zero width arises from zero observed discordance in the pilot (not evidence of a true zero-variance effect).
optional_revisions: Provide the deterministic verifier implementation (or pseudocode) and a compatibility test that others can run, or include a short appendix figure showing verifier decision branches.

If feasible, rerun a small targeted set of more challenging tasks (or adversarially perturbed intents) to demonstrate the pipeline's sensitivity and increase informative discordant outcomes — label any additional runs exploratory.
Include a short explicit reproducibility appendix with step-by-step artifact retrieval and exact commands to reproduce primary analysis from archived files (point to execution/ path and hashes).

Report any secondary-verifier or simulator-audit comparisons planned in the preregistration (e.g., cross-verifier disagreement counts) and include those numbers or explain why they were not produced in the pilot.
